title: Quantifying Symptom Causality in Clinical Decision Making: An Exploration Using CausaLM
abstract: arXiv:2503.19394v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Current machine learning approaches to medical diagnosis often rely on correlational patterns between symptoms and diseases, risking misdiagnoses when symptoms are ambiguous or common across multiple conditions. In this work, we move beyond correlation to investigate the causal influence of key symptoms-specifically "chest pain" on diagnostic predictions. Leveraging the CausaLM framework, we generate counterfactual text representations in which target concepts are effectively "forgotten" enabling a principled estimation of the causal effect of that concept on a model's predicted disease distribution. By employing Textual Representation-based Average Treatment Effect (TReATE), we quantify how the presence or absence of a symptom shapes the model's diagnostic outcomes, and contrast these findings against correlation-based baselines such as CONEXP. Our results offer deeper insight into the decision-making behavior of clinical NLP models

translated_title: 量化临床决策中的症状因果性：基于CausaLM的探索
translated_abstract: 当前用于医学诊断的机器学习方法往往依赖于症状与疾病之间的相关性模式，当症状模糊或在多种疾病中普遍存在时，存在误诊风险。在这项工作中，我们超越相关性分析，研究关键症状——特别是“胸痛”——对诊断预测的因果影响。利用CausaLM框架，我们生成了有效“遗忘”目标概念的反事实文本表示，从而能够有原则地估计该概念对模型预测疾病分布的因果效应。通过采用基于文本表示的平均处理效应方法，我们量化了症状的存在与否如何影响模型的诊断结果，并将这些发现与CONEXP等基于相关性的基线方法进行对比。我们的结果为临床NLP模型的决策行为提供了更深入的洞察。
tldr: 本研究利用CausaLM框架和TReATE方法量化了关键症状（如胸痛）对临床诊断模型预测结果的因果效应，超越了传统基于相关性的分析方法，为理解临床NLP模型的决策机制提供了新途径。
en_tdlr: This study leverages the CausaLM framework and Textual Representation-based Average Treatment Effect (TReATE) to quantify the causal effect of key symptoms (e.g., chest pain) on clinical diagnostic model predictions, moving beyond correlation-based analysis to provide deeper insight into clinical NLP decision-making.
